msg: QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES is a restricted permission: Play Console asks for the App visibility declaration and accepts it only for eligible use cases (browsers, launchers, security, device management). Otherwise list the packages you need under <queries> instead.
MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (All files access) needs the All files access declaration in Play Console and a core-functionality justification; file pickers and scoped storage are expected instead.
ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION triggers the Location permissions declaration: Play wants the feature that needs background location, a video of it, and a prominent in-app disclosure before the request.
SMS and Call Log permissions are restricted: Play grants them mainly to the app the user has set as default handler, and every other use needs the Permissions declaration with an approved exception.
REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES has its own Play declaration: say which files you install and why, or the update is rejected as unapproved app distribution.

Broad photo and video access needs the Photo and video permissions declaration: Play expects the Android photo picker for one-off or infrequent access, and broad access only where it is core functionality.
Health Connect read or write permissions need the Health apps declaration form approved before release, plus a privacy policy that names the health data you read.
From Android 14 USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT is granted at install only to calling and alarm apps; everything else must justify it to Play and fall back gracefully when the user has turned it off.
USE_EXACT_ALARM is restricted to alarm clock and calendar apps; if that is not your app Play expects SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM with a user-facing setting, or WorkManager.

form: Exact alarm use case (Play policy answer)
msg: SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM is not granted by default on Android 13 and later: check canScheduleExactAlarms() and send the user to the Alarms and reminders setting, and keep the use case ready for review.
Declaring AD_ID means the Data safety form must disclose that the app collects the advertising ID and for what purpose; the two answers are cross-checked at review.
An accessibility service is bound here: Play requires a prominent in-app disclosure of what the service reads and does, and rejects accessibility use that is not an accessibility feature.
Each foregroundServiceType in the manifest needs a matching use case in the Play Console foreground service declaration, with a video showing the service running.
Android 14 (API 34) throws SecurityException when a foreground service starts with a type whose FOREGROUND_SERVICE_* permission is missing from the manifest.
foregroundServiceType="specialUse" needs a <property android:name="android.app.PROPERTY_SPECIAL_USE_FGS_SUBTYPE"> inside the same <service>, and Play reviews that subtype string by hand.
